items.definition: A horizontal row in the periodic table; elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.
items.sentence: Sodium and chlorine are in the same [blank], period 3 of the periodic table.

items.definition: A vertical column in the periodic table; elements in the same group have the same number of outer electrons and similar properties.
items.sentence: Lithium, sodium, and potassium are all in [blank] 1 of the periodic table.

items.definition: An element on the left and centre of the periodic table; typically shiny, conducts electricity, and forms positive ions.
items.sentence: Iron is a [blank] that is magnetic and can conduct electricity.

items.definition: An element on the right side of the periodic table; typically poor conductors and form negative ions or covalent bonds.
items.sentence: Chlorine is a [blank] that forms a diatomic molecule and is a yellow-green gas.

items.definition: An element in Group 1 of the periodic table; very reactive metals that form +1 ions.
items.sentence: Sodium is an [blank] that reacts vigorously with water to form a hydroxide solution.

items.definition: An element in Group 7 (17) of the periodic table; non-metals that form diatomic molecules and react to gain one electron.
items.sentence: Chlorine is a [blank] that exists as a diatomic gas at room temperature.

items.definition: An element in Group 0 (18) of the periodic table; inert gases with full outer electron shells.
items.sentence: Helium is a [blank] that is used in balloons because it is lighter than air and unreactive.

items.definition: An element in the central block of the periodic table; typically hard, dense, good conductors with variable oxidation states.
items.sentence: Iron is a [blank] that can form ions with different charges, such as Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺.

items.definition: How readily an element reacts with other substances; increases down Group 1 and decreases down Group 7.
items.sentence: The [blank] of alkali metals increases as you go down Group 1.

items.definition: Dmitri Mendeleev, the scientist credited with creating the first widely accepted version of the periodic table.
items.sentence: [Blank] arranged elements by atomic mass and left gaps for undiscovered elements.

items.definition: An energy level around the nucleus where electrons are found, determining an element's period and reactivity.
items.sentence: The number of occupied [blank]s tells you which period an element is in.

items.definition: A one- or two-letter abbreviation for an element used in chemical formulae and equations.
items.sentence: The chemical [blank] for sodium is Na and for iron is Fe.

items.definition: A reaction in which a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive element in a compound.
items.sentence: Chlorine displaces bromide in a [blank] reaction because it is more reactive.

items.definition: A reaction in which an atom or ion loses electrons (in terms of electron transfer) or gains oxygen.
items.sentence: [Blank] occurs when iron loses electrons to form Fe²⁺ ions.

items.definition: A reaction in which an atom or ion gains electrons or loses oxygen.
items.sentence: [Blank] occurs at the cathode during electrolysis when positive ions gain electrons.

items.definition: The process by which an atom gains or loses electrons to form an ion.
items.sentence: Group 1 metals undergo [blank] easily because their outer electron is far from the nucleus.

items.definition: The proportion of a particular isotope of an element found in a natural sample.
items.sentence: The relative atomic mass of chlorine is calculated using the [blank] of its two isotopes.

items.definition: A characteristic of an element or compound, such as melting point, conductivity, or reactivity.
items.sentence: Elements in the same group share similar chemical [blank]s.

items.definition: A pattern of change in properties across a period or down a group in the periodic table.
items.sentence: The [blank] in reactivity down Group 1 can be explained by the increasing number of electron shells.

items.definition: The most reactive halogen, in Group 7; a pale yellow diatomic gas at room temperature.
items.sentence: [Blank] is the most electronegative element and the most reactive of the halogens.
